newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Strike closes airport in riot-torn Guiana.
newsitem.headline: Strike closes airport in riot-torn Guiana.

text.p: A general strike in riot-torn French Guiana has closed the international airport near the capital Cayenne, airport officials told Reuters on Wednesday.
They said all incoming and outgoing flights had been cancelled for the day.
Air France said it had cancelled flights from Paris and the French West Indies.
Wednesday's closure was the second time in a week that the airport had been closed because of labour unrest.
The strikes followed four nights of rioting in Cayenne this month.

The riots were sparked by a strike of high school students protesting at poor conditions in local schools, but the students' protest was soon overtaken by more radical groups, some of whom favour French Guiana's independence from mainland France.

Last week, one person died and at least 20 were injured during four nights of rioting in the capital Cayenne. The violence caused millions of dollars in damage to property -- mostly government buildings and shops.

France's Education Minister Francois Bayrou and Overseas Territories Minister Jean-Jacques de Peretti were in Guiana negotiating with local politicians, labour unions and student groups. The two arrived on Tuesday.
Paris has sent more than 500 paramilitary riot police to Cayenne, a city of 35,000, in recent days.
French Guiana lags behind mainland France in housing, education and health. Official unemployment exceeds 23 percent and young people are the hardest hit.
